larrikin.name: The Larrikin
larrikin.blurb: You shorten everything, tease your mates and treat slang like a second language. If a word has three syllables, you've already made it two and added an -ie on the end.

barista.name: The Flat White Local
barista.blurb: Your Aussie is relaxed and friendly. You know your coffee order by heart, say thanks to the bus driver and keep the slang gentle. People find you easy to talk to.
say: Can I grab a flat white, thanks?

yarner.name: The Bush Yarner
yarner.blurb: You'd rather have a long chat than a short one. Your Aussie is dry, practical and full of stories, with a slow rhythm and a good sense of humour.

beachie.name: The Beach Local
beachie.blurb: Everything's easygoing with you. Your Aussie is loose and friendly with plenty of 'yeah' and 'nah'. You'd turn up to a wedding in your best thongs.

pro.name: The Office Legend
pro.blurb: You switch smoothly between work English and weekend English. You keep emails clear, make small talk before meetings and drop in a 'no worries' at the right moment.
say: Let's touch base in the arvo.

questions.q: A friend says "How ya going?" What do you say?
It's Saturday morning. Where are you?
opts: At a café with a flat white
At a mate's place, planning a barbie
Thongs, obviously, and what's wrong with 'em?

questions.q: Your boss asks if you can stay late. You say:
Which sentence sounds most like you?
opts: "Could I get a long black, please?"
"Let me check my calendar and confirm."

questions.q: You're in a long queue. What do you do?
opts: Chat to the stranger behind me
Make a joke about how long it is
Enjoy the sun, it's all good
Fish and chips on the sand

questions.q: Someone does you a favour. You say:
opts: "Thanks so much, I really appreciate it."
